meta.title: Pitch graph | E. Berke Karagöz
meta.description: Live pitch of your microphone and of audio playing in another tab, on one graph.

intro.title: Pitch graph
intro.description: Live pitch of your mic, and of any tab you share.

controls.label: Inputs
controls.headphones: Use headphones, otherwise the mic also picks up the tab.

graph.ariaLabel: Pitch over the last 8 seconds. The mic is the blue line, the shared tab the orange line, the mic's nearest note the green band.

errors.micDenied: Microphone access is blocked. Allow it in the site settings and retry.
errors.micBusy: The mic couldn't be opened. Another app may be using it, or the system may be blocking it (on Windows: Settings › Privacy & security › Microphone). Fix that and retry.
errors.noTabAudio: The tab was shared without audio. Share it again with “Also share tab audio” ticked.
errors.tabUnreadable: The browser couldn’t capture that audio. This happens with some app windows. Share a browser tab instead.
errors.unsupported: Tab audio sharing only works in desktop Chrome and Edge.
errors.insecure: The browser only allows the mic and tab sharing on https or localhost. This page is open over plain http.

warnings.echoCancellation: Echo cancellation is still on. Readings may be less steady.
warnings.noiseSuppression: Noise suppression is still on. Quiet notes may drop out.
warnings.autoGainControl: Automatic gain is still on. Loudness may jump.

use.title: How to use it
use.inputs: Press “Start mic” and allow the microphone. To add another tab's audio, press “Share a tab” and tick “Also share tab audio” in the browser's dialog. Use headphones, otherwise the mic also picks up the tab.
use.graph: The graph shows the last 8 seconds, with note names on both sides. The blue line is the mic and the orange line is the shared tab; the faint shading behind each line is its spectrum. The green band is the note nearest to the mic. A line gets thicker and slightly brighter as the sound gets louder, and fades a little when it is very quiet. The bar at the right edge shows the level of the mic in blue and of the tab in orange, in dBFS, relative to your microphone or the tab audio, with a tick for the level where the mic's pitch detection switches on.
use.readout: The readout gives the mic's note, how far it is from the nearest note in cents, and its frequency in Hz. At the end it gives the mic's level in dBFS; a dash means silence. A check mark appears within 15 cents.
use.view: “Range” sets how many octaves are visible. Drag the bar under the graph to change its height. “Full screen” shows only the tool.

works.title: How it works
works.plain: The page measures the pitch of the sound many times a second and draws each result. It follows one pitch per source, between 65 and 1100 Hz, and leaves a gap where it finds none. For a shared tab it first keeps what is the same in the left and right channels, where a lead vocal usually sits, and removes the bass.
works.detail: The analysis runs in your browser. An AudioWorklet passes the samples to a Web Worker, which finds pitch candidates with the YIN method. A tracker then picks the most likely line through them and smooths it.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.audio: The audio is analysed on your device. The page does not record it or send it anywhere. It keeps only the last few seconds of results in memory, to draw the graph.
privacy.video: Browsers only share a tab's audio together with its video. The page stops the video as soon as sharing starts and does not use it.
privacy.storage: The tool saves two settings in the browser's local storage: the graph height and the range.
privacy.site: Ads and analytics on this site are covered separately:

support.title: Browser support
support.mic: The mic needs your permission, and browsers only allow it on pages opened over https or localhost. If access is blocked, allow it in the site settings and retry.
support.tab: Tab audio needs a desktop Chromium browser such as Chrome or Edge. In other browsers the “Share a tab” button is disabled.
support.processing: The page asks the browser to turn off echo cancellation, noise suppression and automatic gain. If one stays on, a note appears under the buttons. The “Full screen” button appears only where the browser supports it.
